beats.text: The man who saw the 1859 flare doubted it caused the storm.
beats.note: Richard Carrington wrote that one swallow does not make a summer.

beats.name: Carrington and Hodgson
beats.role: Two British astronomers who saw the flare independently, just before noon on 1 September.

beats.text: The aurora was reported close to the equator.
beats.note: Sightings came from Cuba, Hawaii and Colombia, far further south than usual.

beats.text: Telegraph equipment shocked operators and threw sparks.
beats.note: NOAA also records small fires, and messages arriving that no one had sent.

beats.context: Two operators between Boston and Portland worked with their batteries disconnected, powered by the sky alone.

beats.text: He saw it first and doubted it most.

beats.line: Science is slower than the sky.
